design.text: Randomized, double-blind, 18-center, 6-month international trial comparing two uncontrolled pasireotide dose regimens (600 µg bid vs 900 µg bid)

citations.quote: Pivotal study B2305 was a randomized, Phase III, 18-center, 6-month, double-blind, international clinical trial that assessed the safety and efficacy of two pasireotide dose regimens: 600 µg bid and 900 µg bid in patients with Cushing's disease.
Given that Study B2305 was an uncontrolled clinical trial, the efficacy analyses focus on changes from baseline to end-of-trial for different efficacy variables.

population.text: Adult Cushing's disease patients with persistent/recurrent hypercortisolism despite prior pituitary surgery, or de novo patients who were poor surgical candidates; baseline 24-hour UFC >1.5 x ULN

citations.quote: Study B2305 enrolled adult patients with Cushing's disease who demonstrated persistence of hypercortisolism despite prior pituitary resection or had recurrence of hypercortisolism after an initial favorable response to surgery. *De novo* Cushing's disease patients were allowed enrollment only if they were poor surgical candidates because of general bad health, if they had surgically unapproachable tumors, or if they refused surgery.

Patients with a baseline 24-hour urine free cortisol (UFC) >1.5 x upper limit of normal (ULN) were randomized to receive a SIGNIFOR dosage of either 0.6 mg subcutaneous b.i.d. or 0.9 mg subcutaneous b.i.d..

endpoint.text: Proportion of responders at Month 6 (mean 24-hour UFC normalized to ≤ ULN without a dose increase during the period), assessed by individual dose group

citations.quote: In Study B2305, the pre-specified primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of responders at Month 6 by individual dose group (pasireotide 600 µg s.c. bid or 900 µg s.c. bid) in the Full Analysis Set (FAS) consisting of all randomized patients who received at least one dose of pasireotide.
The primary efficacy endpoint was the proportion of patients who achieved normalization of mean 24-hour UFC levels after six months of treatment and did not dose increase during this period.

n.text: 162 randomized patients dosed (82 in the 600 µg bid group, 80 in the 900 µg bid group)

citations.quote: Of the remaining 162 randomized patients, 82 were in the 600 \mug bid group and 80 in the 900 \mug bid group.

result.text: UFC responders at Month 6: 15% (12/82) in the 600 µg bid group and 26% (21/80) in the 900 µg bid group. The 900 µg dose met the primary efficacy criterion (lower bound of two-sided 95% CI = 17%, exceeding the 15% non-inferiority margin); the 600 µg dose did not.

citations.quote: At Month 6, the percentages of responders for the primary endpoint were 15% and 26% in the 0.6 mg b.i.d. and 0.9 mg b.i.d. groups, respectively (Table 3).
The 900 µg dose met the primary efficacy criterion (lower bound of the two-sided 95% CI equal to 17% and greater than the non-inferiority margin of 15%) but the 600 µg dose did not.

indication.text: Treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative

citations.quote: SIGNIFOR is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with Cushing's disease for whom pituitary surgery is not an option or has not been curative.

target_moa.text: Cyclohexapeptide somatostatin analogue that binds and activates somatostatin receptors (notably hsst5, frequently over-expressed on corticotroph tumor cells), inhibiting ACTH secretion and thereby decreasing cortisol secretion

citations.quote: SIGNIFOR is an injectable cyclohexapeptide somatostatin analogue. Pasireotide exerts its pharmacological activity via binding to somatostatin receptors (sst).

Corticotroph tumor cells from Cushing's disease patients frequently over-express hsst5 whereas the other receptor subtypes are often not expressed or are expressed at lower levels. Pasireotide binds and activates the hsst receptors resulting in inhibition of ACTH secretion, which leads to decreased cortisol secretion.
SIGNIFOR is an injectable cyclohexapeptide somatostatin analogue.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (overall, N=162) were diarrhea (58%), nausea (52%), hyperglycemia (40%), cholelithiasis (30%), headache (28%), abdominal pain (24%), fatigue (19%), and diabetes mellitus (18%). Hyperglycemia/diabetes is a key risk; 5% of patients had ALT or AST >3x ULN; injection site reactions occurred in 17%.

summary.text: Signifor was reviewed under Standard (not priority) review, received February 17, 2012, with orphan drug designation (granted 2009). It was presented to the EMDAC advisory committee on November 7, 2012 (unanimous 'yes' vote) and approved first cycle in 2012 for Cushing's disease, with three post-marketing requirements (registry, spontaneous-report analysis, and a hyperglycemia-management trial).

description.text: Fulfilled postmarketing requirement with Study CSOM230B2219 on managing Signifor-induced hyperglycemia and updated section 6 of labeling

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for the POSTMARKETING REQUIREMENT 1985-3: "A multi-center, randomized, clinical trial investigating the management of Signifor (pasireotide)-induced hyperglycemia in patients with Cushing's disease treated with Signifor", as stated in the approval letter dated December 14, 2012.
